name: Interpolation Search
description: Improved binary search that estimates the target's position using a formula similar to how humans search a phone book — probe where the value is likely to be based on its magnitude.
aim: Search sorted array by estimating position: probe = low + (target-arr[low])/(arr[high]-arr[low]) × (high-low). Adjust search range based on comparison.
howItWorks: Estimate probe position using linear interpolation formula
If arr[probe] < target: search right (low = probe+1)
If arr[probe] > target: search left (high = probe-1)

time.bestCase: Target at exactly the interpolated position

realWorld: Searching uniformly distributed data like timestamps
Phone book lookups — page estimate based on alphabetical position
Searching large sorted numeric datasets with uniform distribution
whenToUse: Sorted array with uniformly distributed values
Large datasets where O(log log n) matters
alternatives: Binary Search — guaranteed O(log n), no assumptions about distribution
Hash Tables — O(1) average for exact matches
